question.problem: If $\operatorname{tan}⁡x=10,$ for some value of $x,$ find the value of $\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tan}⁡(x-3\pi ).$
question.worked_solution:
The period of $y=\operatorname{tan}⁡x$ is $\pi .$ Therefore, for any integer $n,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\operatorname{tan}⁡(x+n\pi ).
$$

Substituting $n=-3$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\operatorname{tan}⁡(x+(-3)\cdot \pi )=\operatorname{tan}⁡(x-3\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Since $\operatorname{tan}⁡x=10,$ we get that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(x-3\pi )=10.$ Therefore

$$
\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tan}⁡(x-3\pi )=\frac{1}{2}(10)=5.
$$
